prior_art.title: SpecBench: Measuring Reward Hacking in Long-Horizon Coding Agents
prior_art.authors: Bingchen Zhao, Dhruv Srikanth, Yuxiang Wu, Zhengyao Jiang
prior_art.metadata_verified: direct fetch of arxiv.org/abs/2605.21384 on 2026-08-06 (title/authors/id/category/date all confirmed)
prior_art.fetched_quote: As long-horizon coding agents produce more code than any developer can review, oversight collapses onto a single surface: the automated test suite. Reward hacking naturally arises... the agent optimizes for passing tests while deviating from the user's true goal. We... decompose software engineering tasks into three parts: (i) a natural language description of the specification (ii) visible validation tests... and (iii) held-out tests that compose those same features to simulate real-world usage... we use the gap in pass rates on these two suites to quantify reward hacking... SpecBench, a benchmark comprising 30 systems-level programming tasks... every frontier agent saturates the visible suite, reward hacking persists.

collision.why: SpecBench IS a coding-agent (cs.SE) benchmark that isolates reward-hacking/spec-gaming via the visible-vs-heldout pass-rate gap, published 2026-05-20, ~3 months BEFORE this paper (2026-08-04). It falsifies NC8's universal 'NO current coding-agent benchmark isolates specification-gaming defense' and directly refutes the supporting reasoning ('all... silent on Axis B') — SpecBench's contribution is precisely that the gap IS the Axis-B signal.
collision.salvage: The collision is on SCOPE/SWEEP, not method. SpecBench uses an OBSERVATIONAL gap metric; NC8 proposes an adversarial INJECTION attack set — different methods. NC8 is salvageable IF narrowed to a methodology-novelty claim ('no benchmark uses an adversarial injection-attack-set methodology') AND SpecBench is cited as the concurrent benchmark that already isolates spec-gaming observationally.
collision.required_amendment: (1) §8.3/§5: cite SpecBench (arXiv:2605.21384) as concurrent prior art; (2) retract the universal 'No benchmark currently isolates specification-gaming defense' → 'No benchmark uses an adversarial injection-attack-set methodology; the concurrent SpecBench isolates spec-gaming observationally via a visible-vs-heldout gap metric'; (3) reframe the contribution as the injection-set method, not the existence of any isolating benchmark.

NC5's binary is 'proxy-INTEGRITY (auditable diff-tampering) vs proxy-ADEQUACY (non-auditable fit-to-intent)' over coding loops, paired with a defense-reach impossibility claim. Different axes, different domains.

clear_under_search.caveat: Clear-under-search means NO collision found in the searched corpus (bounded: ~6 targeted queries across arXiv/web/repos on 2026-08-06), NOT 'novel'. The two-layer search-oracle weakness applies: (1) selection-side — ranking/recall limits, the found text is model-extracted from search returns; (2) comparison-side — the claim-vs-prior-art match is model-judged. NC1/NC2/NC3 (framing claims) are the weakest 'clear' results because a framing could exist in work the bounded search did not reach; NC4/NC6/NC7 (specific schema/mechanism claims) are stronger. A broader formal search could shrink the clear set.
